text:
Mira (runtime): quick brain-dump — proposing a "burst shaping" + admission proto for dedicated GPU pools to reduce cold-start cost while keeping p95 latency tight. RFC: https://rwd.co/rfc/burst-shaping
Jon P: high-level: how is "shaping" different from existing burst-lane credits?
Mira (runtime): burst lanes are all-or-nothing slots. shaping is continuous: we allow fractional token consumption per tenant and throttle upstream requests smoothly instead of hard-rejects. goal: fewer sudden evictions and more predictable latency.
Samira: sounds promising. can you sketch the accounting surface? how do we prevent a noisy tenant consuming shaped headroom?
Mira (runtime): two parts: 1) local admission in proxy that enforces per-tenant flow-rate + short-window token bucket, 2) central ledger operator that reconciles credits and issues ephemeral prewarm slots. proxy uses weighted shaping based on priority class.
Kai (SRE): main concern: p95 spikes during rewarm. shaping helps, but if many tenants rewarm simultaneously we'll still see infra pressure. need backpressure signal from operator -> autoscaler.
Mira (runtime): agreed. plan: operator exposes a simple intent metric stream: available_prewarms, headroom_utilization, inflight_evictions. autoscaler subscribes and reacts with staged scale-up (quick small step + follow-up) instead of single big scale.
Jon P: can we have a config example?
Mira (runtime): sure, here's a minimal autoscaler policy snippet:
```yaml
policy: burst-shape-v1
shaping:
  window_ms: 5000
  max_fraction: 0.25   # max of tenant RPS that can consume shaped headroom
  min_reserve: 0.05    # guaranteed baseline
operator:
  reconcile_interval: 10s
  prewarm_granularity: 2gpus
  staged_scale:
    step: 0.2   # fraction of pool to add per stage
    cooldown: 30s
observability:
  emit: [p95_latency, headroom_util, prewarm_queues]
```
Samira: nice. does `max_fraction` apply per-tenant or per-tenant-class?
Mira (runtime): per-tenant-class by default, overridable per-tenant for enterprise customers.
Kai (SRE): also add a safety circuit: if p99 > X ms for 30s, short-circuit shaping and prioritize stability (i.e., use reserved capacity only).
Mira (runtime): good call — add that as an emergency policy in operator.
Jon P: operator vs proxy ownership question: who enforces credit deduction? if proxies are stateless, we need a low-latency path to the ledger.
Mira (runtime): ledger writes are eventual for accounting; proxy keeps a local token cache and periodically syncs. critical path decisions use the cache only, with conservative refill heuristics to avoid overspend. operator reconciliation fixes drift and can revoke tokens when needed.
Samira: we should simulate with real tenant mixes. I'll spin up a small sim with bursty traffic and 80/20 tenants. expected outputs: fewer evictions, lower p95 variance, slightly higher prewarm cost.
Mira (runtime): awesome — ping me the sim results and I'll draft a short follow-up RFC section with configs and operator API.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: autoscaler-proto branch -> staging (CI ok) :rocket:
Kai (SRE): one last ask — add an operator metric for "revoked_tokens" so we can alert on ledger churn.
Mira (runtime): noted, will add. thanks all :thumbsup:
